None of these perform network access, download code, or exfiltrate data.

The `source` array declares upstream URLs (github.com git and release archives), but `makepkg --printsrcinfo` does not download or verify sources at this step. The two `eval` statements at the end only dynamically define shell functions (`package_onnxruntime-provider-cuda...` and `package_onnxruntime-provider-tensorrt-cuda...`); they do not execute package-build logic, access the network, or write files. No `curl`, `wget`, `base64`, or obfuscated payloads appear at top level. All suspicious content is confined to function bodies (`prepare`, `build`, `package`) which do not run during this gate.

Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this file is safe.
</details>
